summary_paragraph: A woman with a recent history of aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting presented with brief episodes of palpitations and left-sided chest pain. She had been recovering at home but developed symptoms accompanied by a non-productive cough. Evaluation revealed stable vital signs, no significant pericardial effusion, and EKG changes attributed to left ventricular hypertrophy rather than acute ischemia. A chest X-ray showed new left lower lobe collapse, likely contributing to her discomfort. She remained in normal sinus rhythm, tolerated hemodialysis without issue, and responded well to pain management and respiratory support. Her medications were adjusted, including restarting isosorbide mononitrate at a lower dose and increasing metoprolol. With symptom resolution and stable condition, she was discharged home on the second day with instructions for wound care, activity restrictions, and follow-up appointments.
